itemListElement.name: Restaurant Marketing Ideas That Bring Local Customers Through the Door

mainEntity.name: What is the best marketing for a small restaurant?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no single best channel. For most independent restaurants, the foundation is a complete Google Business Profile, real photos, steady reviews with replies and a website that answers a hungry guest's questions quickly. Paid ads and email or text lists come after that.

mainEntity.name: How do I get more customers for my restaurant locally?

acceptedAnswer.text: Be easy to find, easy to trust and easy to choose. Keep your Google listing accurate, show real photos, ask every guest for a review and reply to what people write. Then make it simple to reserve, order or call.

mainEntity.name: Can I pay Google to rank my restaurant higher on the map?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Google says there is no way to request or pay for a better local ranking. You can complete your profile, earn reviews and keep your information accurate, but you cannot buy the position.

mainEntity.name: Can I offer a discount in exchange for a Google review?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Google classes offering free or discounted goods or services in exchange for reviews as fake and misleading content, and it is strictly prohibited. Ask every guest the same way and let the review be honest.

mainEntity.name: Should my restaurant menu and profile be in more than one language?

acceptedAnswer.text: If a meaningful share of your guests read another language, yes. Write dish names and short descriptions for the people who will read them, instead of translating word for word, and reply to reviews in the language they were written in when you can do it well.
